title: DLMF 24.10 Arithmetic Properties: Here and elsewhere in § 24.10 the symbol p denotes a prime number.
summary: DLMF 24.10 Arithmetic Properties: Here and elsewhere in § 24.10 the symbol p denotes a prime number.
body: NIST DLMF section 24.10 (Arithmetic Properties) says: "Here and elsewhere in § 24.10 the symbol p denotes a prime number. where the summation is over all p such that p-1 divides 2n . The denominator of B_{2n} is the product of all these primes p . where n\geq 2 , and \ell(\geq 1) is an arbitrary integer such that (p-1)p^{\ell}\mathbin{|}2n . Here and elsewhere two rational numbers are congruent if the modulus divides the numerator of their difference. valid when m\equiv n\pmod{(p-1)p^{\ell}} and n\not\equiv 0\pmod{p-1} , where \ell(\geq 0) is a fixed integer. valid for fixed integers \ell(\geq 0) , and for all n(\geq 0) and w(\geq 0) such that 2^{\ell}\mathbin{|}w . Let B_{2n}=\ifrac{N_{2n}}{D_{2n}} , with N_{2n} and D_{2n} relatively prime and D_{2n}>0 . Then where M(\geq 2) and b are integers, with b relatively prime to M . For historical notes, generalizations, and applications, see Porubský ( 1998 ) . valid for fixed integers \ell(\geq 1) , and for all n(\geq 1) such that 2n\not\equiv 0 \pmod{p-1} and p^{\ell}\mathbin{|}2n ." Equation 24.10.1 on the page has alt text "B_{2n}+\sum_{(p-1)\mathbin{|}2n}\frac{1}{p}=\hbox{integer},". Equation 24.10.2 on the page has alt text "pB_{2n}\equiv p-1\pmod{p^{\ell+1}},". This card records that section's wording and equation alt text. It does not retypeset a formula the alt text did not carry.
